intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise
experiences.description: Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Enjoy breathtaking Hawaiian sunsets, spot sea turtles and dolphins, and experience the ocean breeze while avoiding peak daytime heat. Many operators include snacks and drinks.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show
experiences.description: Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This indoor and covered-venue experience showcases the traditions, music, and dance of six Pacific Island cultures, making it ideal for families and perfectly timed to avoid daytime heat.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking
experiences.description: Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours before temperatures peak. Paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands, spot sea turtles, and enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters. Equipment and safety gear are included in the rental.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Collect luggage, pick up any pre-booked rental car or take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, ~$3/ride) to your accommodation. Check in or store luggage if room isn't ready yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Ala Moana Beach Park (free entry) — a calm, family-friendly beach perfect for a relaxed first afternoon. Let the kids splash in the protected waters while you soak in the Hawaiian sun. Grab shave ice from a nearby stand to cool off.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Ala Moana Center (open-air mall nearby) for window shopping and to get your bearings. Grab an affordable dinner at the Ala Moana Food Court featuring local plate lunch options.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport upon arrival — look for local options like a musubi (spam rice ball) for ~$2-3
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Kapahulu — famous local plate lunches for ~$10-12 per person
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center Food Court — try L&L Hawaiian Barbecue for a classic plate lunch dinner under $12

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the midday arrival. Pick up a TheBus pass or grab a Biki bike share day pass ($15) for affordable local transport. Stop at a grocery store like Foodland to stock up on snacks and breakfast items to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots. Arrive early (opens 6:45 AM) to beat crowds and secure entry ($25/adult, kids under 13 free). Watch the free marine education video before snorkeling among colorful fish and coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free) — a 2-mile round-trip paved hike with stunning ocean views. Families with kids will love spotting sea turtles and whales (seasonal) from the clifftop lookout.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kailua Town for a relaxed evening walk. Browse local boutiques and grab a casual dinner at a local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased yesterday — cereal, fruit, and juice
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from your grocery haul to eat at Hanauma Bay picnic area
meals.dinner: Kailua Town — try Kalapawai Cafe & Deli for fresh sandwiches and local fare around $12-15

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online (book at least 2 days ahead). Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required by Hawaii law). Snorkel gear can be rented at the bay for ~$12. August weather averages 16.8°C highs — bring a light layer for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — Hawaii's most iconic volcanic crater hike. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail is manageable for families and rewards hikers with panoramic Honolulu views. Entry is $5/person or $10/car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Waikiki Beach (free) — the world-famous stretch of sand is perfect for swimming, building sandcastles, and people-watching. Rent a bodyboard (~$10/hour) for some family fun in the waves.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki for the lively evening atmosphere. Watch free hula and live music performances often held at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly around 6:30 PM).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery — a Hawaii institution at ~$1.50 each
meals.lunch: Waikiki — try Marugame Udon for fresh udon noodles starting at $7, a budget-friendly and filling option
meals.dinner: Musubi Cafe Iyasume near Waikiki for affordable Hawaiian-Japanese fusion — meals under $10

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head opens at 6:00 AM — going early avoids heat and crowds. Bring water and sunscreen. The Kuhio Beach hula show is free and a wonderful cultural experience for the whole family. Parking in Waikiki can be expensive — use TheBus instead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (PCC) in Laie on the North Shore. Purchase the basic admission package (~$60/adult, ~$48/child) which includes access to 6 Polynesian village exhibits. Spend the morning exploring Samoa, Fiji, Tonga, Hawaii, Tahiti, and Aotearoa villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring PCC — watch live cultural demonstrations including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving. Kids will love the interactive activities. Enjoy the included canoe pageant on the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the evening 'Ha: Breath of Life' luau show at PCC (included in some packages or add-on ~$20 extra). It's a spectacular family-friendly performance with fire dancing and Polynesian storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack fruit and granola bars for the drive to the North Shore
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant inside PCC — all-you-can-eat buffet included in some packages or ~$25 separately
meals.dinner: PCC luau dinner buffet (if attending the show) or stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck on the way back (~$14 for a plate)

day_by_day.notes: PCC is about a 1-hour drive from Honolulu. Book tickets online in advance for discounts. This is one of the pricier days but offers exceptional cultural and entertainment value for families. Look for Costco or AAA discount packages to save up to 20%.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the North Shore to visit Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) — a stunning crescent beach with calm summer waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Walk up to the famous Waimea Bay rock jump (for older kids and adults).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along Kamehameha Highway stopping at Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline) — iconic surf spots that are calm and swimmable in summer. Explore the Haleiwa Town area with its charming surf shops and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Haleiwa — browse the historic town and watch the sunset over the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from hotel groceries to eat on the road
meals.lunch: Haleiwa — Matsumoto Shave Ice is legendary (~$4-6) plus grab a plate lunch from a nearby food truck
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens or Kono's Northshore for affordable burritos and local fare (~$12-15)

day_by_day.notes: North Shore beaches are significantly calmer in summer (August) than winter — ideal for family swimming. The drive along the North Shore is scenic and free. Bring a cooler with drinks and snacks to save money. August can have occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial (free, but timed entry passes required — book online in advance) is a must-see. Arrive early as passes go quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center exhibits (free) and walk the grounds. If budget allows, add the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum (~$27/adult, ~$14/child) for an interactive family experience inside a real WWII submarine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu and explore Chinatown — a vibrant neighborhood with street art, local markets, and affordable dining options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up fresh pastries from a local bakery en route
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to eat at Pearl Harbor's picnic area — no outside food allowed inside the memorial but permitted in the parking/picnic zones
meals.dinner: Honolulu Chinatown — Little Village Noodle House for authentic Chinese-Hawaiian cuisine, meals ~$10-14

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is free but the boat ride to the USS Arizona Memorial requires advance timed-entry reservations at recreation.gov. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed — leave bags in the car. This is a solemn and educational experience appropriate for children 6 and older.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Manoa Falls Trail — a lush, jungle-like hike through a rainforest leading to a beautiful 150-foot waterfall. The 1.6-mile round trip is family-friendly and costs ~$5 parking. Wear water shoes as the trail can be muddy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lyon Arboretum (free or small donation) adjacent to the trailhead — 194 acres of tropical plants, orchids, and native Hawaiian species. Kids will love the exotic plants and peaceful setting.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kapiolani Park near Waikiki for a free evening picnic. The park often hosts free community events, concerts, and sports activities on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or smoothie bowls from a local cafe — look for deals around $8-10
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and fruit for a picnic at the arboretum
meals.dinner: Kapahulu Avenue — try Ono Hawaiian Foods for authentic local Hawaiian cuisine (laulau, poi, kalua pig) under $15

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls trail can be slippery — wear closed-toe shoes with grip. The rainforest microclimate means this area gets more rain than the coast, so a light rain jacket is recommended. Mosquito repellent is a must for the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches. The powdery white sand and turquoise water are perfect for families. Rent kayaks (~$25/hour for a double) to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lanikai neighborhood — a quiet, upscale residential area with a beautiful beach and the famous Lanikai Pillbox Hike (free, ~1 mile round trip) offering breathtaking views of the Mokulua Islands and coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu and visit the Aloha Tower Marketplace at the historic harbor for a relaxed evening stroll and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Kailua Town — Cinnamon's Restaurant for famous Hawaiian pancakes and local breakfast, ~$12-15
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua for fresh deli sandwiches and local snacks, ~$10-12
meals.dinner: Aloha Tower Marketplace — Gordon Biersch Brewery Restaurant for happy hour deals or nearby food trucks

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach has free parking but it fills up quickly — arrive before 9 AM. The Lanikai Pillbox hike is short but steep in places — manageable for kids 8 and older. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. The beach has no lifeguards so supervise children closely.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Exhibits cover Hawaiian royalty, natural history, and Pacific Island cultures. Admission is ~$25/adult, ~$17/child. The planetarium show is an extra highlight for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Punchbowl Crater (National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific) — free to visit and offers panoramic views of Honolulu. A peaceful and historically significant site with beautiful grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Honolulu — return to Waikiki for a sunset beach walk and farewell dinner. Browse the International Market Place for last-minute affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up fresh fruit and pastries from Chinatown's Oahu Market
meals.lunch: Bishop Museum Cafe or pack a lunch to eat on the museum grounds
meals.dinner: Waikiki — Duke's Waikiki for a splurge-worthy farewell dinner with ocean views (appetizers and happy hour deals available to keep costs reasonable, ~$20-25/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is excellent for families with children — interactive exhibits and the Science Adventure Center are particularly engaging. Look for online discount codes or AAA discounts before purchasing tickets. The Punchbowl is free and a respectful, beautiful stop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely sunrise walk on Waikiki Beach or Ala Moana Beach Park. Collect any last shells, take final photos, and enjoy the peaceful early morning Hawaiian atmosphere before the beach crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation and head to the airport. Allow extra time for traffic and airport security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts. Grab a final plate lunch at the airport's local food options.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii — carry the aloha spirit home! Review your trip highlights and start planning your next Hawaiian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab a smoothie and acai bowl from a beachside vendor for a true Hawaiian farewell
meals.lunch: Honolulu International Airport — Makai Market Food Court for affordable local options including poke bowls and plate lunches
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — arrange late checkout if possible or store luggage at the hotel. Honolulu Airport (HNL) recommends arriving 3 hours before international/mainland flights. Use any remaining grocery items for a final picnic breakfast to minimize waste and save money.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim. Check-in and freshen up after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip ahead. Rest and recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Downtown Disney District or a nearby family-friendly area for a relaxed first evening. Explore the shops and enjoy the atmosphere without overexerting after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or quick bite at the airport terminal upon arrival
meals.dinner: Claim Jumper Restaurant & Bar near Buena Park — hearty American comfort food at mid-range prices, great for families after a travel day

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM local time, Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest and hydration. Confirm any pre-booked Hawaii activity reservations and review the upcoming itinerary. Note: The hotel is located in Buena Park, California — this itinerary assumes a connecting or multi-leg journey to Hawaii beginning Day 2 or that Hawaii activities are accessed via day trips/island hopping from a California base. Activities listed from Day 3 onward reflect the Hawaii experiences available.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hotel breakfast and final packing. Depart hotel for LAX or John Wayne Airport (SNA) for the connecting flight to Hawaii (Honolulu or Maui). Arrive in Hawaii mid-morning to early afternoon depending on flight schedule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Upon arriving in Hawaii, check into your island accommodation (pre-booked mid-range hotel such as an Outrigger or Courtyard by Marriott property near Waikiki). Drop bags and head straight to Waikiki Beach for your first taste of Hawaiian sand and surf. Enjoy a casual swim and beach walk along the iconic shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Watch the stunning Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean while enjoying light refreshments on board. Perfect introduction to Hawaii for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast at SureStay before departure
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or grab a plate lunch from a local Hawaiian spot near Waikiki such as Rainbow Drive-In — a beloved local institution with affordable loco moco and plate lunches
meals.dinner: Light snacks provided on the catamaran cruise; follow up with dinner at Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with fresh fish, burgers, and Hawaiian classics at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Book the Waikiki Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance as spots fill quickly, especially in August. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, light layers for the evening breeze on the water, and a camera for sunset photos. August weather averages around 16.8°C with some rain — evenings on the water can be breezy so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking — Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours. Paddle through crystal-clear turquoise waters, spot sea turtles, and explore the scenic Mokulua Islands offshore. The guided experience is suitable for all skill levels including young children.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, relax on Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches. Build sandcastles, snorkel in the calm waters, or rent stand-up paddleboards from a local vendor. Explore the charming Kailua Town with its boutique shops and local art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area. Enjoy a relaxed evening walk along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's main strip. Browse local shops and pick up souvenirs. Watch street performers near the Waikiki Beach Walk.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their red velvet pancakes and Hawaiian-style breakfast; a local favorite and perfect pre-kayaking fuel
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market & Deli in Kailua — grab fresh sandwiches, salads, and local snacks for a casual beach picnic after kayaking
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — incredibly popular, affordable, and delicious Japanese udon noodle restaurant; expect a short line but worth every minute

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is approximately 30–40 minutes from Waikiki by car. Rent a car or book a rideshare for the day. Morning kayaking tours typically begin at 8:00–9:00 AM to beat the heat and wind. Book the kayaking tour at least 2–3 days in advance. Bring water shoes, sunscreen, and a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits — Visit Hawaii's largest and most celebrated museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, Science Adventure Center, and planetarium. Ideal for families with children of all ages and a great rainy-day option given August's rainfall averages.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, drive to Punchbowl Crater (National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific) for a short, meaningful visit and panoramic views of Honolulu. Then head to Ala Moana Beach Park for a relaxed afternoon swim and beach time at one of Oahu's largest and most family-friendly beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show — Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie. This spectacular production features fire dancing, traditional music, and the stories of Polynesian peoples. A must-see family experience in Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery — a Honolulu institution since 1950, famous for their coco puffs and classic American-Hawaiian breakfast plates at very reasonable prices
meals.lunch: Café on-site at Bishop Museum — convenient and reasonably priced; or pack a lunch from a nearby Foodland grocery store
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Buffet included with the Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show package — a generous spread of Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes including kalua pig, poi, haupia, and fresh fish

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is located in Laie on the North Shore, approximately 1 hour from Honolulu. Plan to arrive by 5:00–5:30 PM for the luau dinner before the 7:30 PM show. Book tickets well in advance — August is peak season. The Bishop Museum opens at 9:00 AM. Allow 2.5–3 hours for a thorough visit. This is an excellent day if rain is expected as both major activities are largely indoors or covered.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning drive to the North Shore of Oahu. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park for a scenic walk and photo stop — in summer the waters are calm and perfect for swimming. Continue to Haleiwa Town, the charming surf village of the North Shore, for a morning stroll through local shops and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Haleiwa further — visit the Haleiwa Farmers Market if available, or stop at Dole Plantation for a family-friendly pineapple maze adventure and the famous Dole Whip frozen treat. Tour the plantation grounds and learn about Hawaii's pineapple history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hotel pool or take a sunset walk along Waikiki Beach. Visit the Waikiki Aquarium (open until 4:30 PM — adjust timing if needed) or simply enjoy the beachfront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa — famous for their breakfast burritos stuffed with kalua pork, eggs, and rice; a North Shore staple
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — the legendary North Shore shrimp truck serving garlic butter, spicy, and lemon shrimp plates; an iconic Hawaii food experience
meals.dinner: Hy's Steak House Waikiki or Yard House at Waikiki Beach Walk — mid-range options with great variety for families; Yard House offers an extensive menu with something for everyone

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore drive from Waikiki takes approximately 45–60 minutes. A rental car is strongly recommended for this day. Dole Plantation is conveniently located on the way back from the North Shore to Waikiki. In August, North Shore waves are small and calm — ideal for family swimming. Keep an eye on weather as August can bring afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight to Maui (approximately 30–40 minutes from Honolulu). Check into your Maui accommodation (mid-range option: Courtyard by Marriott Maui Kahului Airport or a condo rental in Kihei). Head to Ka'anapali Beach — one of Maui's most famous stretches of golden sand — for a morning swim and snorkel session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, sharks, and coral reef ecosystems. The walk-through underwater tunnel is a highlight for families. Located in Ma'alaea Harbor, it's one of the finest aquariums in the United States.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Lahaina Town (historic waterfront district) for an evening stroll under the famous 150-year-old Banyan Tree. Browse the art galleries, street performers, and waterfront shops. Watch the sunset from the Lahaina Harbor waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the Honolulu airport before your inter-island flight, or stop at Maui's Tasty Crust Restaurant in Kahului — a beloved local diner open since 1944 with fluffy pancakes and local-style breakfasts
meals.lunch: Café on-site at Maui Ocean Center — convenient and family-friendly; or grab plate lunches from a nearby local spot in Ma'alaea
meals.dinner: Lahaina Fish Co. — waterfront dining in historic Lahaina with fresh local fish, seafood pasta, and beautiful ocean views at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines well in advance. August is peak travel season and flights sell out. Maui Ocean Center is open daily from 9:00 AM — plan to spend 2–3 hours. The aquarium is an excellent option if afternoon rain arrives. Lahaina's historic district is walkable and very family-friendly in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the iconic Road to Hana drive — one of Hawaii's most spectacular scenic routes. Stop at Twin Falls for a short family-friendly hike to beautiful waterfalls. Continue along the winding coastal road with stops at Garden of Eden Arboretum and Ke'anae Peninsula overlook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Wai'anapanapa State Park — home to the famous black sand beach, sea caves, and dramatic lava coastline. Swim in the unique black sand cove (check conditions) and explore the coastal trail. Arrive in Hana Town for a brief rest.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive back toward your Maui accommodation (or stay overnight in Hana if budget allows — Travaasa Hana is a splurge option). Enjoy a quiet evening back at the hotel, reviewing photos from the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Pack a picnic breakfast from a Kahului grocery store (Safeway or Whole Foods) the night before — the Road to Hana starts early and options are limited along the route
meals.lunch: Halfway to Hana Stand — a beloved roadside fruit stand offering fresh banana bread, tropical fruit smoothies, and local snacks; a Road to Hana tradition
meals.dinner: Hana Ranch Restaurant in Hana Town — casual, locally-sourced burgers and plates; or if returning to Kihei, try Kihei Caffe for a relaxed dinner

day_by_day.notes: Start the Road to Hana no later than 7:00–8:00 AM to avoid traffic and have enough time at each stop. The full round trip takes 8–10 hours. A rental car is essential. Download an offline map or use the Shaka Guide Road to Hana audio tour app for family-friendly narration. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations for parking — book online before the trip. Bring rain gear as this area receives significant rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling at Molokini Crater — book a guided snorkel boat tour departing from Ma'alaea Harbor. This partially submerged volcanic crater is one of Hawaii's top snorkeling destinations with exceptional visibility and abundant marine life including tropical fish, rays, and sea turtles. Most tours depart at 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the snorkel tour (typically back by noon–1:00 PM), relax at Wailea Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful and calm resort beaches. Enjoy the afternoon sun, build sandcastles, and take a walk along the Wailea Beach Path connecting several stunning beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset at Makena Beach (Big Beach) — Maui's largest white sand beach with dramatic scenery. Watch the sun dip below the horizon before heading back for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the early snorkel departure — most tour operators provide light snacks and beverages on board; grab a banana and granola bar from the hotel
meals.lunch: Monkeypod Kitchen in Wailea — excellent farm-to-table burgers, fresh fish tacos, and local craft beers in a lively, family-friendly atmosphere at mid-range prices
meals.dinner: Kō Restaurant at Fairmont Kea Lani — a slightly elevated mid-range dinner experience celebrating Hawaii's plantation-era culinary heritage with fresh local ingredients and beautiful presentation

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini snorkel tour at least 1 week in advance — tours with companies like Pride of Maui or Trilogy Excursions are highly rated and family-friendly. Most tours include snorkel gear, instruction, and light refreshments. August conditions are generally calm and excellent for snorkeling. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — required in Hawaii by law.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakalā National Park — Drive up to the summit of Haleakalā volcano (10,023 feet elevation) for breathtaking above-the-clouds views. Explore the visitor center, learn about the unique silversword plants, and walk the short Pā Ka'oao (White Hill) trail for panoramic crater views. Note: Bring warm layers — summit temperatures can be near 10°C even in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakalā and stop in Upcountry Maui — visit Surfing Goat Dairy for a fun family farm tour and goat cheese tasting, or explore the charming town of Makawao with its paniolo (Hawaiian cowboy) heritage, boutique shops, and local bakeries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Maui coast. Enjoy a final Maui evening at Ka'anapali Beach watching the cliff divers at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — a free nightly tradition where a torch lighter dives from the lava rock into the ocean at sunset, honoring ancient Hawaiian tradition.

meals.breakfast: Kula Lodge Restaurant in Upcountry Maui — a cozy mountain lodge restaurant with stunning views and hearty breakfasts; perfect stop on the way up to Haleakalā
meals.lunch: Grandma's Coffee House in Keokea — a beloved Upcountry institution serving homemade soups, sandwiches, and locally grown Maui coffee in a charming setting
meals.dinner: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village, Ka'anapali — oceanfront dining with fresh seafood, steaks, and Hawaiian classics; great views and family-friendly atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā National Park requires advance reservations for summit access — book through recreation.gov well before your trip. The park entrance fee is $30 per vehicle. Dress in warm layers — temperatures at the summit are significantly cooler than the coast. The drive from Kihei to the summit takes approximately 1.5 hours. Upcountry Maui is a wonderful contrast to the beach experience and highly recommended for families.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last swim at your Maui beach. Pack up and check out of accommodation. If time allows before your flight, visit the Maui Arts and Cultural Center or browse the Maui Swap Meet at the University of Hawaii Maui College for local crafts, fresh produce, and unique souvenirs at very affordable prices (open Saturday mornings — adjust if schedule permits).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Maui via inter-island flight back to Honolulu, then connect to your mainland flight home. Allow ample time for airport check-in and security. Pick up any last-minute gifts at the Honolulu Duty Free or airport shops — Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and Hawaiian sea salt make excellent souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Homeward bound — reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with beaches, culture, family memories, and aloha spirit.

meals.breakfast: Café des Amis in Paia Town (if routing through North Maui) — charming café with crepes, smoothie bowls, and excellent coffee; or hotel breakfast for a relaxed final morning
meals.lunch: Airport dining at Kahului Airport — L&L Hawaiian Barbecue for a final plate lunch of kalua pork, macaroni salad, and rice; an affordable and authentic farewell meal
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dining at Honolulu International Airport — Makai Market Food Court offers a variety of local and international options for a layover meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all return flight times and allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for inter-island connections and mainland check-in. Maui's Kahului Airport (OGG) is well-organized but busy in August. Ensure all reef-safe sunscreen, macadamia nuts, and fresh fruit comply with agricultural inspection rules when returning to the mainland — declare all food items. Take a moment at the airport to soak in the last views of the beautiful Hawaiian mountains and say mahalo for an unforgettable trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise
experiences.description: Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Enjoy breathtaking Hawaiian sunsets, spot sea turtles and dolphins, and experience the ocean breeze while avoiding peak daytime heat. Many operators include snacks and drinks.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show
experiences.description: Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This indoor and covered-venue experience showcases the traditions, music, and dance of six Pacific Island cultures, making it ideal for families and perfectly timed to avoid daytime heat.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking
experiences.description: Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours before temperatures peak. Paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands, spot sea turtles, and enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters. Equipment and safety gear are included in the rental.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to your luxury accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your hotel and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll along the nearest beach to acclimate to the island atmosphere. Enjoy the warm Hawaiian sun and turquoise waters at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Watch the stunning Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean while enjoying light refreshments on board.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant offering fresh Hawaiian seafood and island-inspired cuisine with stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion dining experience with premium sushi and signature black cod dishes

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule light to allow for jet lag recovery and settling in. Confirm catamaran cruise booking in advance as sunset slots fill up quickly in August.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking — Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours. Paddle through crystal-clear waters and explore the scenic coastline, with expert guides ensuring a safe and memorable experience for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Kailua Beach — one of Hawaii's most pristine white-sand beaches. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, snorkel in the calm turquoise waters, and enjoy the natural beauty of the windward coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area for a relaxed evening. Explore the upscale shops at Royal Hawaiian Center and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant at the Ilima Hotel — famous for their fluffy pancakes and local Hawaiian breakfast favorites
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Café & Deli in Kailua — beloved local spot with gourmet sandwiches, fresh salads, and artisan coffee
meals.dinner: The Pig and the Lady — award-winning Honolulu restaurant blending Vietnamese and Hawaiian flavors with locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is approximately 30–40 minutes from Waikiki. Book kayaking tour in advance. August mornings are ideal for kayaking before afternoon trade winds pick up.

day_by_day.morning: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits — Visit Hawaii's largest and most prestigious museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Polynesian culture. Explore the iconic Hawaiian Hall, planetarium shows, and hands-on science exhibits perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chinatown Honolulu — wander through the vibrant historic district, visit local art galleries, fresh markets, and boutique shops. Take a guided walking tour to discover the rich cultural heritage of this unique neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show — Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Enjoy a premium luau dinner package with traditional Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, and Fijian performances.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things — iconic Honolulu breakfast spot famous for their macadamia nut pancakes and fresh tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Lucky Belly — trendy Chinatown restaurant known for creative ramen, bao buns, and Asian-fusion small plates
meals.dinner: Polynesian Cultural Center Ali'i Luau — premium all-inclusive luau dinner with traditional Hawaiian cuisine including kalua pig, poi, and haupia

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is located on the North Shore, approximately 1 hour from Honolulu. Book the premium 'Ali'i Luau' package well in advance. The evening show runs approximately 2.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: North Shore Adventure — Visit the legendary Sunset Beach and Banzai Pipeline. Even in August (off-season for big waves), the beaches are beautiful and calm, perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Explore the charming Haleiwa town with its surf shops and local art galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dole Plantation Visit — Tour the historic pineapple plantation, ride the Pineapple Express train, and navigate the world's largest outdoor maze. Sample fresh pineapple products and enjoy the lush tropical surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the iconic House Without a Key at the Halekulani Hotel, featuring live Hawaiian music and hula dancing.

meals.breakfast: Café Haleiwa — legendary North Shore breakfast spot beloved by surfers and locals for hearty omelets and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck — iconic North Shore food truck serving world-famous garlic shrimp plates
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani — Hawaii's most acclaimed fine dining restaurant offering exquisite French-Hawaiian cuisine with panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: North Shore is approximately 1 hour from Waikiki. August is the calm season on the North Shore, making it ideal for families. Reserve La Mer well in advance — it is one of Honolulu's most sought-after dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Diamond Head Crater Hike — Embark on a guided family hike up the iconic Diamond Head volcanic crater. The moderate 1.6-mile round-trip trail rewards hikers with breathtaking panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Start early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve Snorkeling — Visit this world-renowned marine sanctuary for a premium snorkeling experience. The protected bay is teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles in crystal-clear waters, perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Magic Island (Ala Moana Beach Park) — Enjoy a peaceful sunset at this beautiful lagoon park. Stroll along the waterfront and watch the sky transform into brilliant shades of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Heavenly Island Lifestyle — organic, farm-to-table breakfast spot near Waikiki with acai bowls, avocado toast, and fresh tropical smoothies
meals.lunch: Roy's Hawaii Kai — legendary Hawaiian fusion restaurant by celebrity chef Roy Yamaguchi, located near Hanauma Bay
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia Waikiki — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's stunning oceanfront restaurant featuring innovative Asian cuisine and premium sushi

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges an entry fee. Arrive early at Diamond Head (opens at 6 AM) to avoid crowds and heat. Snorkeling equipment rental is available at Hanauma Bay.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui — Take an early morning flight from Honolulu to Kahului, Maui (approximately 35 minutes). Check in to your luxury Maui resort and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, sharks, and coral reef ecosystems. The open-ocean tunnel and touch pools are especially popular with families.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Kaanapali Beach — Stroll along the famous Kaanapali Beach boardwalk and witness the traditional cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock (Puu Kekaa), a beloved Maui tradition performed at sunset.

meals.breakfast: In-flight snack or quick bite at Honolulu Airport's premium lounge
meals.lunch: Maui Ocean Center Seascape Restaurant — casual waterfront dining with fresh seafood and stunning harbor views
meals.dinner: Merriman's Kapalua — farm-to-table fine dining by celebrated chef Peter Merriman, featuring locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients with spectacular ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights in advance. Hawaiian Airlines and Southwest offer frequent Honolulu–Maui routes. Arrange luxury resort transfer from Kahului Airport. Maui Ocean Center is located in Maalaea, approximately 20 minutes from Kaanapali.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana Luxury Tour — Embark on a guided private luxury tour along the legendary Road to Hana. Stop at Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, and the stunning black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park. A professional guide handles all driving so the family can fully enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana experience — visit the sacred Pools of Oheo (Seven Sacred Pools) at Kipahulu, hike through bamboo forests, and discover hidden waterfalls along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Maui resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy the resort's infinity pool and spa facilities as the sun sets over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Gazebo Restaurant in Napili — beloved Maui breakfast spot with ocean views, famous for macadamia nut pancakes
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by your private tour guide — gourmet Hawaiian-style bento boxes with fresh local fruits and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House — Maui's most iconic and celebrated restaurant, featuring ultra-fresh fish caught daily by local fishermen in a stunning beachfront setting

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles with over 600 curves and 59 bridges. A private guided tour is strongly recommended for families. Book Mama's Fish House weeks in advance — it is one of the most sought-after reservations in all of Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakala Sunrise Tour — Wake before dawn for a guided luxury tour to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 feet). Watch the spectacular sunrise above the clouds from the crater rim — a truly once-in-a-lifetime experience. Dress warmly as summit temperatures can be near 10°C.
day_by_day.afternoon: Upcountry Maui Exploration — Visit the charming town of Makawao, explore local art galleries, and tour a lavender farm or pineapple plantation. Enjoy the cooler upcountry temperatures and lush green landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Wailea Beach Sunset — Relax on the pristine shores of Wailea Beach, one of Maui's most beautiful luxury resort beaches. Enjoy a beachside cocktail as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast provided by your tour operator before the Haleakala sunrise departure
meals.lunch: Hali'imaile General Store — legendary upcountry Maui restaurant by chef Bev Gannon, serving creative Hawaiian regional cuisine in a historic plantation building
meals.dinner: Spago Maui at Four Seasons Resort Wailea — Wolfgang Puck's acclaimed restaurant featuring California-Hawaiian cuisine with stunning ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala National Park requires advance reservations for sunrise viewing — book months ahead as spots are extremely limited. Bring warm layers as summit temperatures are significantly cooler than sea level. The sunrise tour departs around 3 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Molokini Crater Snorkeling Cruise — Board a premium catamaran for a morning snorkeling excursion to Molokini Crater, a partially submerged volcanic caldera teeming with marine life. The crystal-clear waters offer visibility up to 150 feet, making it one of the world's top snorkeling destinations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wailea Beach Afternoon — Return to your resort for a relaxing afternoon on the beach. Enjoy premium beach service, paddleboarding, or a rejuvenating spa treatment at your resort's world-class spa.
day_by_day.evening: Old Lahaina Luau — Attend the most authentic and celebrated luau in all of Hawaii. Enjoy traditional Hawaiian food, storytelling, and hula performances in an intimate oceanfront setting in historic Lahaina town.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the early morning snorkeling departure
meals.lunch: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman in Wailea — casual upscale dining with farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine, craft cocktails, and live music
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — traditional Hawaiian feast included with luau package, featuring kalua pig, lomi salmon, poi, and haupia coconut pudding

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini snorkeling cruise and Old Lahaina Luau well in advance — both are extremely popular and sell out quickly. The luau is held outdoors; light layers are recommended for the evening breeze. Check weather conditions as August can bring occasional afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning at Kaanapali Beach — Enjoy a leisurely last morning on Maui's stunning Kaanapali Beach. Take a final swim, collect shells, or simply relax with a tropical drink and soak in the breathtaking scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir Shopping and Departure Preparation — Visit the Shops at Wailea for premium Hawaiian gifts, local artwork, and luxury souvenirs. Pack and prepare for departure, checking out of your resort with ample time for the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight from Kahului Airport back to the mainland. Reflect on an unforgettable 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with world-class beaches, cultural experiences, and family memories.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore — beloved Maui breakfast spot famous for their slow-roasted kalua pork breakfast burritos and fresh tropical smoothies
meals.lunch: Lahaina Grill — sophisticated fine dining in historic Lahaina featuring innovative New American cuisine with Hawaiian influences — a perfect farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — consider picking up fresh poke bowls from a local market to enjoy at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Kahului Airport is approximately 45 minutes from Kaanapali. Consider shipping any large souvenir purchases home to avoid baggage fees. Confirm return flight details and arrange luxury resort transfer in advance.
